starting_points.name: rails new PostgreSQL application
starting_points.when: A new server-rendered Rails application with the normal Hotwire stack.
steps: Install/select a supported Ruby and Rails version, Bundler, PostgreSQL and the native prerequisites for the pg gem; record versions.
Inspect rails new help. Generate the full application with PostgreSQL; keep Hotwire and test/security defaults unless the actual brief requires an exception.
Configure development/test credentials through environment or ignored configuration, then prepare the intended development database.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Create the conventional Rails application and PostgreSQL configuration.

commands.cwd: The generated my_app directory, after database configuration
commands.purpose: Prepare the intended local database and schema.

notes: Replace my_app with the intended unused Rails name. The normal generator initializes Git without committing; review any custom application templates for extra effects.

Do not add --skip-git just to avoid a commit: it also skips generated .gitignore/.gitattributes. Rails defaults already include Turbo/Stimulus; do not install a separate SPA or skip Hotwire without a product reason.

follow_up_generators.name: Authentication
follow_up_generators.when: A new application needs Rails built-in session authentication and has not already selected another identity solution.

commands.purpose: Generate session authentication support using the installed Rails version.

commands.cwd: The generated my_app directory, after reviewing the new migrations and database target
commands.purpose: Apply the generated authentication migrations locally.

notes: Inspect bin/rails generate authentication --help first. Implement signup, mail configuration and per-resource authorization deliberately; generated login is not a complete product identity policy.

follow_up_generators.name: Model or scaffold
follow_up_generators.when: A new domain resource is required; choose a model for custom workflows or scaffold when generated CRUD screens fit.

commands.purpose: Generate an example model with migration and test/fixture support.

notes: Product and name:string are examples; replace them with the actual domain design. Review constraints and indexes before migrating.
Alternative: bin/rails generate scaffold Product name:string generates CRUD layers as well; choose it instead of generating the same model twice. Inspect generator help or --pretend before writes.

follow_up_generators.name: Additive migration
follow_up_generators.when: An existing Product model/table needs the example description column.

commands.cwd: The generated my_app directory with an existing Product table
commands.purpose: Generate a migration for an existing resource.

notes: Review the generated migration before bin/rails db:migrate; do not edit a migration already shared/applied to disguise a later schema change. Names/attributes are examples.

preserve: Generated .gitignore/.gitattributes, binstubs, Gemfile.lock, database configuration, credential exclusions, test/fixture layout, Hotwire/import-map setup and generated security/CI checks.
Do not replace generated Rails defaults with a small handwritten skeleton; record brief-driven omissions and additions.
verification: Inspect bin/rails generate and the relevant generator --help for the installed version.
Run database migration status, bin/rails zeitwerk:check, domain/system tests and generated security/style checks that are present.
Run the generated server and inspect a browser journey; authentication/authorization still require behavior tests.

sources.title: Rails getting started, authentication and Hotwire
Rails application generator source: Git and ignore-file behavior

integration_steps: Configure ignored development/test database credentials and prepare the intended databases using the generated configuration. Use the conditional authentication generator when login is required; implement signup and resource-level permissions deliberately.

If Pundit is the selected authorization library, add it through Bundler and run bin/rails generate pundit:install after reviewing installed help; implement and invoke policies rather than relying on authentication alone.
Start bin/rails server and inspect a browser journey. Configure Solid Queue using the installed-version guide and run its bin/jobs worker only when background work is required and enabled.
Preserve Gemfile.lock and the generated checks. Add bundler-audit in development only if it is required and absent. Define authorization, duplicate-job and migration tests for the features present.

Prepare the chosen deployment configuration, secret ownership, database persistence and backup/restore procedure. When Kamal is the selected host tooling and deployment is authorized, use bundle exec kamal setup for initial setup or bundle exec kamal deploy for a subsequent release.
